checkpoint_finding.declared_training_corpus: Only split-local retained evidence topology, outcome-independent features, and project-generated retained-graph negatives
checkpoint_finding.embedded_upstream_training_corpus: none; selected PyG components and example contain no learned biological checkpoint
checkpoint_finding.source_chronology_interpretation: GraphSAGE's library release carries no biological knowledge. Clean eligibility depends on every project feature and message-passing edge being constructed inside the split.

interpretation: GraphSAGE is the only model in this audit wave that can produce a principled score for a node absent from training topology, and only because the frozen recipe prohibits node-ID embeddings and supplies outcome-independent node features with root_weight=true. This conditional inductive property makes future held-back source recovery technically feasible. It does not make the relation-agnostic projection typed, and there is no current held-back source, so no best-model claim is available.
known_incidents_and_biases: GraphSAGE is not inherently leakage-proof or inductive. A trainable node-ID table, full-graph degree feature, target-derived roster, or target-derived attribute would make the project model transductive or contaminated.

LinkNeighborLoader documents that supervision edges are not masked from message passing by default. Every held-source, held-block, and validation edge must be physically removed before loader construction and verified by sampled global edge IDs.

LinkNeighborLoader's native approximate negative sampling can produce false negatives. The project recipe disables it and supplies type-compatible negatives constructed without held outcomes; hidden positives may still occur and cannot be repaired by peeking.
Root-only isolated nodes with the same allowed features receive identical embeddings. A finite score is not evidence of locus-specific information; root-only results require a separate stratum.

The registered homogeneous projection discards relation types, edge direction, source-native weights, and multiplicity. Node-type features and candidate filtering do not turn it into R-GCN, HGT, or a typed transformer.
Retained-source degree and observation channels are graph derivatives. Computing or scaling them on the full graph before source/block removal is direct leakage.

Training positives may also be present in retained message-passing topology, following the upstream graph-autoencoding example. This cannot be used as a validation score and never permits a validation or held edge in message passing.
Raw dot products require development-only calibration for Brier score. Source-specific recalibration after a sealed source is opened is prohibited.
MIT source terms do not establish redistribution rights for a state trained on restricted graph features.
remaining_blockers: Promote the corrected 50-study COLOC release, then freeze a graph snapshot, ontology, provenance families, native-build block map, source-independent candidate roster, full feature schema/order, and explicit missingness states.
Resolve rights for every topology and feature source and decide whether graph-derived trained states may be redistributed; otherwise restrict release to code, manifests, hashes, and predictions.

Implement split-local feature construction and scaling, typed negative controls, homogeneous edge projection, LinkNeighborLoader wrapper, global-edge leakage receipts, and root-only/untestable coverage exports.

Freeze an exact Python, PyTorch, torch-geometric, sampler-extension, CPU/CUDA, driver, wheel, deterministic, and seed environment; pass CPU and optional L40S import, forward/backward, sampler, state-load, resume, cross-device, and tolerance probes on SLURM.

Pass synthetic fixtures proving that held-source, deterministic derivative, held-block, and inner-validation edges never enter features, negatives, normalization, caches, message passing, early stopping, or calibration.

Create five immutable states per split and hash graph, roster, x, masks, scaler, negatives, sampler order, environment, state, raw predictions, calibrator, coverage, resources, and terminal disposition.
Prospectively register a wholly sealed evidence source and freeze its source-independent feature handoff before outcomes. Until then all GraphSAGE findings are development-only.
